questions.question: How much notice does the Brightwater supply agreement require to terminate for convenience?
questions.raw_output: The documents conflict on this point. The Agreement says either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving ninety (90) days' written notice to the other. The Amendment states that except as expressly amended, the Agreement continues in full force and effect, including the notice period for termination for convenience. However, a later memo summarising the terms states that either party must give sixty (60) days' written notice.

questions.question: What uptime has Orion committed to, per the contract documents?
questions.raw_output: The documents conflict on Orion's uptime commitment. The SLA states that Orion commits to a monthly Platform availability of 99.9%, measured across each calendar month at the Orion ingest gateway and excluding Scheduled Maintenance. The Pricing Schedule instead states that for the purposes of this Pricing Schedule, Orion's committed Platform uptime is 99.5% per calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance. Both documents are marked as in force, and none of the provided documents says which figure takes precedence.

questions.question: How long do we have to keep contractor invoices and maintenance work orders?
questions.raw_output: The documents conflict on this point. The operations memo says maintenance work orders, contractor invoices and callout sheets held by the operations department shall be kept for five (5) years from the end of the fiscal year in which they were closed, and may then be deleted from the shared drive by the stations supervisor. The Retention Policy says financial records, including general ledgers, payment vouchers, supplier invoices, contractor invoices and maintenance work orders, shall be retained for seven (7) years from the end of the fiscal year in which they were created, and it applies to every employee, contractor and board member who creates or receives records on behalf of the Authority. Both documents are listed as in force, and they also differ on the starting point (closed vs. created), so I can't determine which period governs from these documents alone.
